question: On the Montana Basic Control Skills test, how many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing to check the position of your vehicle?
choice_a: A maximum of two (2)
choice_b: A maximum of one (1)
choice_c: None
choice_d: Unlimited
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing to check the position of your vehicle?
choice_a: Two (2)
choice_b: Three (3)
choice_c: None
choice_d: One (1)
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

question: On which two exercises is "Final Position" of the vehicle scored?
choice_a: Exercise 1 and Exercise 4
choice_b: Exercise 3 and Exercise 4
choice_c: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: Exercise 1 and Exercise 3
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

topic: Basic Control Skills - Completing an Exercise
question: What must you do upon completion of a Basic Control Skills exercise to indicate you are finished?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_b: Wave to the examiner
choice_c: Turn off the engine and exit the vehicle
choice_d: Flash your headlights
explanation: The manual states that upon completion of an exercise you must set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate you have completed the exercise.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

topic: Basic Control Skills - Final Exercise Boundaries
question: When judging whether your vehicle is within final exercise boundaries, which vehicle parts are excluded from consideration?
choice_a: Mirrors and unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck
choice_b: The entire cab
choice_c: Nothing is excluded
choice_d: All tires
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must be within final exercise boundaries other than mirrors and unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height, such as a bucket truck.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

topic: Basic Control Skills - Failure to Follow Instructions
question: What happens if you fail to maneuver your vehicle into the final position exactly as described by the examiner?
choice_a: Nothing, as long as you stay within the outer boundary
choice_b: You are given one extra attempt
choice_c: You receive a warning only
choice_d: You will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
explanation: The manual states that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, you will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

question: Which of the following is given as an example of an "unsafe act" that may cause an automatic failure of the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Asking the examiner for clarification
choice_b: Using a free look on Exercise 2
choice_c: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion
choice_d: Sounding the horn after completing an exercise
explanation: The manual gives forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion as examples of an unsafe act, which may result in automatic failure.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.1 Definitions

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 1 Forward Stop
question: What is the purpose of Exercise 1 - Forward Stop?
choice_a: To demonstrate the ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_b: To demonstrate the ability to offset back and park a vehicle
choice_c: To demonstrate the ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop
choice_d: To demonstrate the ability to maneuver around objects while moving forward
explanation: The manual states that in Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, you will demonstrate your ability to judge the front of your vehicle during a controlled stop.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 1 Forward Stop
question: During Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times are you allowed to stop?
choice_a: As many times as needed to align correctly
choice_b: Two times
choice_c: Three times
choice_d: You may stop only once
explanation: The manual states that during Exercise 1 you drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box, and you may stop only once.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 1 Forward Stop
question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, you will receive points if which of the following occurs?
choice_a: You sound the horn too early
choice_b: The front most part of the vehicle is not in the stop box
choice_c: You shift to neutral before stopping
choice_d: You use a free look
explanation: The manual states you will receive points if the front most part of the vehicle (other than unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height) is not in the stop box.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.1 Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing
question: How does Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing begin?
choice_a: You begin by activating your four-way flashers
choice_b: From a stopped position, you pull forward and stop when the examiner raises their hand
choice_c: You start already inside the alley in reverse
choice_d: You begin by exiting the vehicle to check the alley
explanation: The manual states that from your stopped position from the previous exercise, the examiner will ask you to pull forward and stop when they raise their hand.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing
question: In Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing, when is the maneuver complete?
choice_a: When the rear of the vehicle enters the alley
choice_b: When you have backed for 10 seconds
choice_c: When the examiner honks their own horn
choice_d: When the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley
explanation: The manual states you back straight through the alley until the front of your vehicle has cleared the last set of cones at the far end of the alley.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing
question: What three things are scored during Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, and final position
choice_b: Speed, signal use, and mirror checks
choice_c: Braking smoothness, gear selection, and steering
choice_d: Horn use, seatbelt use, and parking brake use
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and final position during Exercise 2.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 2 Straight Line Backing
question: In Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing, how many free pull-ups are you allowed, and how many times may you exit the vehicle to check around it?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_b: Zero free pull-ups and zero exits
choice_c: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_d: Unlimited pull-ups and one exit
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one (1) free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one (1) time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.2 Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking
question: What does Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking require you to demonstrate?
choice_a: The ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping
choice_b: The ability to parallel park
choice_c: The ability to back a vehicle in a straight line
choice_d: The ability to stop at a precise point
explanation: The manual states Exercise 3 demonstrates your ability to maneuver a vehicle around other objects while moving forward without stopping.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking
question: During Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what must you keep between the cone and the line while steering left through the opening?
choice_a: The front bumper
choice_b: The trailer axle
choice_c: The right-most rear tire
choice_d: The left-most front tire
explanation: The manual states you steer to the left through the opening into the opposite lane, keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking
question: What happens if you stop your vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: You must back up and try again
choice_b: You receive a warning but may continue
choice_c: You are allowed one free stop with no penalty
choice_d: The exercise will be ended
explanation: The manual states you are NOT allowed to stop, back-up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3, and if you stop, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 3 Forward Offset Tracking
question: What two things are scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking?
choice_a: Pull-ups and final position
choice_b: Horn use and parking brake use
choice_c: Encroachments and forward tracking clearance (rear tire between the cone and the line)
choice_d: Speed and steering wheel grip
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for encroachments and forward tracking clearance (rear tire between the cone and the line) on Exercise 3.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.3 Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing
question: What must you demonstrate in Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: The ability to drive forward around objects without stopping
choice_b: The ability to make a controlled forward stop
choice_c: The ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley
choice_d: The ability to merge onto an expressway
explanation: The manual states Exercise 4 demonstrates your ability to offset back and park a vehicle at the end of an alley.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing
question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, how close must the rear most part of your vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within three (3) feet
choice_b: Within ten (10) feet
choice_c: Within one (1) foot
choice_d: It must touch the rear boundary exactly
explanation: The manual states you must bring the rear most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box at the end of the alley.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing
question: If you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4, what must you do?
choice_a: Immediately stop and end the exercise
choice_b: Exit the vehicle and reposition it by hand
choice_c: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise
choice_d: Continue backing further to correct the error
explanation: The manual states if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance until you are signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing
question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, what orientation must the vehicle be in within the alley when completed?
choice_a: Straight within the alley
choice_b: Perpendicular to the alley
choice_c: Facing the outer boundary line
choice_d: Angled at 45 degrees
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must be straight within the alley when completed.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Exercise 4 Reverse Offset Backing
question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: Three free pull-ups and unlimited exits
choice_c: No pull-ups and no exits are allowed
choice_d: One free pull-up and one exit
explanation: The manual states you are allowed two (2) free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, 12.2.4 Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

topic: Basic Control Skills - Road Test Prerequisite
question: According to the manual, what must happen before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: The Basic Control Skills test must be passed
choice_b: You must complete a written re-test
choice_c: You must wait 24 hours
choice_d: You must have a passenger present
explanation: The manual states that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Road Test

question: During the On-Road Driving test, which of the following is a requirement listed by the manual?
choice_a: Exceed the posted speed limit slightly to keep up with traffic
choice_b: Drive only during daylight hours
choice_c: Keep one hand off the wheel at all times
choice_d: Wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must wear your safety belt and obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: To pass the On-Road Driving test, the manual states you must complete the test without what?
choice_a: An accident or moving violation
choice_b: Changing lanes
choice_c: Stopping at any point
choice_d: Using turn signals
explanation: The manual states you must complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not have certain traffic situations, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_b: Retake the test on a different day
choice_c: Skip that portion of the test entirely
choice_d: Drive to a different city to find the situation
explanation: The manual states that if your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate a traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that situation.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, what is "unsafe coasting" while approaching a turn?
choice_a: Coasting for any amount of time
choice_b: Coasting while using the parking brake
choice_c: Coasting downhill only
choice_d: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If you must stop before making a turn, where should you come to a complete stop?
choice_a: Only when another vehicle is present
choice_b: Behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign
choice_c: Anywhere before the intersection
choice_d: In the middle of the intersection
explanation: The manual states you must come to a complete stop behind the stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: If stopping behind another vehicle before a turn, where should you stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_b: Wherever the lane markings end
choice_c: At least one full block behind
choice_d: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap).
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While waiting to make a turn, what should you do with your front wheels?
choice_a: It does not matter as long as you do not roll
choice_b: Turn them toward the direction of the turn in advance
choice_c: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead
choice_d: Turn them away from the direction of the turn
explanation: The manual instructs to keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead while waiting, and also not to let your vehicle roll.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: During the turn itself, what should you continue to check in your mirror?
choice_a: That the fuel gauge is accurate
choice_b: That other drivers are using their signals
choice_c: That your turn signal is flashing
choice_d: That the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn
explanation: The manual states you should keep checking your mirror to make sure the vehicle does not hit anything on the inside of the turn.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: After completing a turn, once you are up to the speed of traffic, what should you do regarding lane position?
choice_a: Use your turn signal and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so, if not already there
choice_b: Remain in whatever lane you finished the turn in
choice_c: Move immediately into the left-most lane
choice_d: Straddle two lanes until the next intersection
explanation: The manual states that after the turn, you should get up to the speed of traffic, use a turn signal, and move into the right-most lane when safe to do so (if not already there).
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: As you approach an intersection, if necessary, when must you come to a complete stop?
choice_a: Only after checking traffic to the left
choice_b: Only if a police officer is present
choice_c: Anywhere within the intersection
choice_d: Behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you, with no coasting
explanation: The manual states that if necessary, you should come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While your vehicle is stopped at an intersection, what must it not do?
choice_a: Have its headlights on
choice_b: Have the parking brake engaged
choice_c: Roll forward or backward
choice_d: Idle for more than 30 seconds
explanation: The manual states your vehicle must not roll forward or backward while stopped at an intersection.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what does the manual say you should NOT do?
choice_a: Yield to pedestrians
choice_b: Change lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Keep your hands on the wheel
choice_d: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions
explanation: The manual states you should not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned and how should its speed be managed?
choice_a: Centered in the left lane, driving slower than traffic
choice_b: As close to parked cars as possible
choice_c: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_d: Straddling the center line to see around traffic
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.3 Urban Business

question: Before changing lanes, what should you do first?
choice_a: Sound your horn to alert other drivers
choice_b: Activate your turn signal only
choice_c: Make the necessary traffic checks, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
choice_d: Accelerate to match the fastest vehicle on the road
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.4 Lane Changes

question: Once on the expressway, what three things must you maintain according to the manual?
choice_a: Four-way flashers, parking brake readiness, and horn use
choice_b: Proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed
choice_c: Radio volume, cabin temperature, and cruise control
choice_d: Constant acceleration, minimum following distance, and left-lane travel
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you should maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing, and vehicle speed.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: When exiting the expressway, once on the exit ramp, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Change lanes to find the fastest exit path
choice_b: Decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_c: Activate your four-way flashers immediately
choice_d: Accelerate to merge back into traffic
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: What is the Stop/Start maneuver intended to simulate?
choice_a: Pulling your vehicle over to the side of the road and stopping as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle
choice_b: Merging onto an expressway
choice_c: A school bus student discharge
choice_d: A railroad crossing stop
explanation: The manual states that for this maneuver you will be asked to pull your vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once your vehicle is fully stopped and out of the flow of traffic, which of the following must you do?
choice_a: Exit the vehicle immediately
choice_b: Cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and shift to neutral or park
choice_c: Turn off the engine completely
choice_d: Leave your feet on the brake and clutch pedals
explanation: The manual states that once stopped you should cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: According to the manual, once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, your vehicle should not be doing which of the following?
choice_a: Blocking driveways, fire hydrants, intersections, or signs
choice_b: Safely out of the traffic flow
choice_c: Parallel to the curb or shoulder
choice_d: Displaying four-way flashers
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should not be blocking driveways, fire hydrants, intersections, signs, etc.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what must you do before turning the steering wheel?
choice_a: Sound the horn three times
choice_b: Turn on the right turn signal
choice_c: Do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves
choice_d: Turn the wheel first, then release the parking brake
explanation: The manual specifically instructs: do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve, when should you reduce your speed?
choice_a: Speed reduction is not necessary for curves
choice_b: Only after exiting the curve
choice_c: Before entering the curve, so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_d: While already in the curve
explanation: The manual states that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: Before reaching a railroad crossing, what should all commercial drivers do regarding trains?
choice_a: Assume no train is coming if none is visible from a distance
choice_b: Only look for trains if crossing gates are down
choice_c: Rely solely on the vehicle's mirrors
choice_d: Look and listen for the presence of trains
explanation: The manual states that before reaching the crossing, all commercial drivers should look and listen for the presence of trains.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: According to the general railroad crossing procedure for all commercial drivers, what must you NOT do while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing?
choice_a: Check traffic in all directions
choice_b: Decelerate before reaching the crossing
choice_c: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_d: Keep both hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states you should not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, at what distance from the nearest rail must you stop at a non-exempt railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 10 feet of the nearest rail
choice_b: Exactly at the rail
choice_c: At least 100 feet away
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states such drivers should stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: As a vehicle displaying placards approaches a railroad crossing, what should the driver activate?
choice_a: The horn continuously
choice_b: The parking brake
choice_c: The four-way flashers
choice_d: The high beam headlights
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, the driver should activate the four-way flashers.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: For a bus operator at a railroad crossing, what may also be required in addition to looking and listening for a train?
choice_a: Reversing away from the crossing
choice_b: Turning off the engine
choice_c: Opening the window and door prior to crossing tracks
choice_d: Exiting the bus to inspect the tracks
explanation: The manual states that if operating a bus, you may also be required to open the window and door prior to crossing tracks.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: What may happen if your test route does not include a railroad crossing?
choice_a: You automatically pass that portion of the test
choice_b: You may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper railroad crossing procedures to the examiner at a simulated location
choice_c: The test is postponed
choice_d: You are given extra points elsewhere
explanation: The manual states that not all driving road test routes will have a railroad crossing, and you may be asked to explain and demonstrate the proper procedures at a simulated location.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass, what might the examiner ask you to tell them?
choice_a: The posted weight limit
choice_b: The speed limit of the next highway
choice_c: The name of the overpass
choice_d: The posted clearance or height
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: After going over a bridge, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The posted weight limit
choice_b: The river or waterway name
choice_c: The number of lanes on the bridge
choice_d: The bridge's construction date
explanation: The manual states that after going over a bridge, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: How far away from the students must a school bus come to a complete stop for a student discharge?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away
choice_b: At least 50 feet away
choice_c: At least 25 feet away
choice_d: Exactly at the curb where students stand
explanation: The manual states the driver must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As you approach the student pick up point, which warning lights and signal should you activate?
choice_a: Hazard flashers only
choice_b: Red warning lights and left turn signal
choice_c: Amber warning lights and right turn signal
choice_d: High beam headlights only
explanation: The manual states that as you approach the student pick up, you must activate amber warning lights and right turn signals.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: When the school bus stops for a student discharge, in addition to placing the transmission in neutral/park and setting the parking brake, what must be activated?
choice_a: The rear-facing camera
choice_b: The amber warning lights only
choice_c: The stop arm and red warning lights
choice_d: The horn continuously
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.10 Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Which of the following clutch practices does the manual specifically warn against?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Using the clutch to shift
choice_c: Double-clutching on unsynchronized transmissions
choice_d: Returning both hands to the wheel after shifting
explanation: The manual states not to ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: According to the manual, when should you avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: On straight sections of highway
choice_b: While going up a grade
choice_c: In turns and intersections
choice_d: While merging onto an expressway
explanation: The manual states not to shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage (for Manual Transmission)

question: According to the manual's brake usage guidance, how should you brake?
choice_a: Ride or pump the brake continuously
choice_b: Brake smoothly using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
choice_c: Use the parking brake for all stops
choice_d: Brake harshly to stop as quickly as possible
explanation: The manual states not to ride or pump the brake, and not to brake harshly; instead, brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.13(c) Brake Usage

question: According to the manual, where should a vehicle finish a left turn on a multiple lane road?
choice_a: In the left-most lane
choice_b: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_c: In any lane that is open
choice_d: Straddling both center lanes
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: Where should a vehicle finish a right turn according to the manual?
choice_a: In the right-most (curb) lane
choice_b: In the center lane
choice_c: In the left-most lane
choice_d: Wherever is most convenient
explanation: The manual states you should finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: According to the manual's lane usage guidance, when should you move to or remain in the right-most lane?
choice_a: Only during urban business driving
choice_b: Unless the lane is blocked
choice_c: Only on expressways
choice_d: Only when instructed by the examiner
explanation: The manual states you should move to or remain in the right-most lane unless the lane is blocked.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.14(d) Lane Usage

question: According to the manual, where should both hands be at all times while driving?
choice_a: One hand on the wheel, one on the gear shift at all times
choice_b: On the wheel only while turning
choice_c: It does not matter as long as the vehicle stays in the lane
choice_d: On the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, then returned to the wheel after the shift
explanation: The manual states to keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting, and once you have completed the shift, return both hands to the steering wheel.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.15 Steering

question: According to the manual, in which types of areas should you scan and check traffic especially closely?
choice_a: Only at railroad crossings
choice_b: Only on the expressway
choice_c: High volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present
choice_d: Only in rural areas
explanation: The manual states you should scan and check traffic in high volume areas and areas where pedestrians are expected to be present.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks

question: According to the manual, when should you check mirrors and traffic relative to an intersection?
choice_a: Only after clearing the intersection
choice_b: Only if a vehicle is signaling
choice_c: Before, while in, and after an intersection
choice_d: Only before entering the intersection
explanation: The manual states you should check mirrors and traffic before, while in, and after an intersection.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 13 - On-road Driving, 13.1.16 Regular Traffic Checks
